scope: July-August 2026 physical-resource tightening sweep across refined products, fertilizer feedstocks, water, agriculture, rubber, soft commodities and industrial metals. Research-only; candidate scores are provisional and do not alter Base Conviction.
coreRead: The strongest common pattern is not generic commodity inflation. It is scarcity moving one layer deeper into processing capacity and enabling inputs: middle-distillate refining, sulphur/sulphuric acid, water distribution and cooling, nitrogen feedstock arbitrage, and natural-rubber acreage/labour. Policy can often relieve the headline commodity faster than it can create the constrained processing layer.

macroCrossCheck.source: Power Stack Macro Pulse v2 / Macro Indicators Dashboard

signals.evidence: ISM Manufacturing Prices 71.1 and Services Prices 70.3 despite softer headline PPI.
signals.implication: Physical input shortages are consistent with survey pricing pressure rather than being isolated commodity spikes.

signals.signal: Refined products are much tighter than crude
signals.evidence: 3-2-1 crack at the 99.6th percentile in the dashboard snapshot, diesel +45.3% YoY, jet fuel +87.0% YoY and refinery utilisation 96.2%.
signals.implication: Refining capacity, not crude availability alone, is the key energy bottleneck.

signals.evidence: Henry Hub around $2.79/MMBtu, -8.5% YoY and -30.3% YTD in the dashboard snapshot.
signals.implication: Low-cost North American nitrogen producers have a feedstock advantage while global fertilizer pricing remains supported by disrupted Gulf supply.

signals.signal: Industrial demand is still expansionary but household demand is weaker
signals.evidence: ISM Manufacturing New Orders 56.7 and Production 58.5 versus weak retail sales and sentiment.
signals.implication: Prefer scarcity beneficiaries with contracted/municipal/industrial demand over discretionary farm-equipment purchases that require strong farmer balance sheets.

cotPositioning.framework: COT is used as positioning context, not as a standalone fundamental signal. COTSignal is useful conceptually because it normalises trader groups versus their one-year range, but the public snapshot available during this sweep was stale at June 9/12, so current CFTC and Investing.com releases were used for July-August positioning.

rankedDivergences.theme: Nitrogen fertilizer: global scarcity versus cheap US gas
rankedDivergences.whyInteresting: Iran/Hormuz disruptions removed millions of tonnes of traded urea/ammonia while Henry Hub remains weak. This creates a margin wedge for efficient North American ammonia/urea producers rather than a generic fertilizer trade.
rankedDivergences.whatCouldBreakIt: Rapid Gulf production/transit normalisation, a spike in US gas, or farmer demand destruction severe enough to overwhelm higher pricing.

rankedDivergences.whyInteresting: Washington can relax gasoline blending rules and add supply quickly, but cannot quickly replace damaged or offline diesel/jet refining capacity. The headline 3-2-1 can therefore fall while the industrial-fuel shortage remains severe.
rankedDivergences.bestExpression: VLO / MPC / PSX rather than generic upstream crude beta
rankedDivergences.whatCouldBreakIt: ULSD crack compresses together with RBOB as Russian/Middle East refinery runs and product inventories normalise.

rankedDivergences.theme: Sulphur is a hidden food-and-metals bottleneck
rankedDivergences.whyInteresting: Nearly half of seaborne sulphur normally moves through Hormuz. Sulphur/sulphuric acid is required for phosphate fertilizer and several hydrometallurgical copper/nickel processes. High phosphate prices therefore do not automatically mean high phosphate-producer margins if sulphur input costs rise faster.
rankedDivergences.bestExpression: Chemtrade Logistics as a North American merchant/regen acid and water-chemicals supplier; avoid treating MOS as a simple fertilizer-price beneficiary
rankedDivergences.whatCouldBreakIt: Normalised Gulf sulphur exports and materially lower acid prices.

rankedDivergences.theme: Water scarcity is colliding with food, power and freight
rankedDivergences.whyInteresting: European drought is simultaneously reducing maize yields, limiting Rhine/Danube freight and curtailing nuclear/hydro output. This is broader than data-centre cooling and creates demand for municipal leak reduction, reuse and water-network efficiency.
rankedDivergences.bestExpression: MWA / XYL / ECL; VMI is longer-duration because farmer affordability is currently weak
rankedDivergences.whatCouldBreakIt: Weather normalisation plus delayed municipal capex; for irrigation equipment specifically, weak farm income can postpone orders even when physical need rises.

rankedDivergences.theme: Natural rubber supply is being cannibalised by palm-oil economics
rankedDivergences.whyInteresting: Indonesia is losing rubber acreage because palm offers better returns and easier labour economics. This is a structural supply removal mechanism rather than a one-season weather shock.
rankedDivergences.bestExpression: Sri Trang Agro-Industry (STA Thailand / NC2 Singapore)
rankedDivergences.whatCouldBreakIt: West African supply growth, weaker tire demand, lower rubber prices, or continued low utilisation at processors.

rankedDivergences.theme: Sugar policy response may export India's shortage to the world market
rankedDivergences.whyInteresting: India authorised 1 Mt of duty-free raw sugar imports after domestic prices rose roughly 40% in two months. Domestic intervention can cap Indian prices while adding a large buyer to the global market; positioning had been net short before the policy shift.
rankedDivergences.bestExpression: Commodity watch first; Brazilian sugar equities require a separate operating/debt screen
rankedDivergences.whatCouldBreakIt: A strong Brazil crop, Indian production recovery or rapid domestic price normalisation.

rankedDivergences.theme: Aluminium physical scarcity is masked by Chinese semi-finished exports
rankedDivergences.whyInteresting: LME inventories fell to a 36-year low and much of the remaining metal is Russian/concentrated, yet Chinese alloy/semi exports are cushioning Western availability and suppressing the headline price signal.
rankedDivergences.bestExpression: Watch primary producers with reliable non-sanctioned supply; requires a valuation and cost-curve screen before promotion
rankedDivergences.whatCouldBreakIt: Gulf smelter recovery, Indonesian additions or continued weak Chinese domestic demand sustaining exports.

stockResearch.theme: Low-cost US nitrogen / global fertilizer scarcity
positiveEvidence: H1 2026 adjusted EBITDA $2.18bn and trailing-12-month free cash flow $1.82bn.
98% of available ammonia capacity operated during the period.
Management estimates the Iran conflict removed roughly 4.0-4.5 Mt of Middle East traded urea and about 1 Mt of ammonia and expects constrained supply into 2027.
Forward P/E around 8x in the Aug 17 market snapshot despite strong 2026 earnings and shareholder returns.
US gas is materially cheaper/looser than the global energy backdrop, supporting feedstock economics.
risks: Stock had already risen more than 50% YTD by mid-August.
Sales volumes are down and farmer demand destruction is real.
US gas costs can rise and Gulf supply can recover faster than expected.
Yazoo City outage and project execution remain company-specific risks.
stockResearch.nextWork: Valuation normalisation against mid-cycle EBITDA, nitrogen price sensitivity and technical entry levels.

stockResearch.theme: Municipal water distribution / leak reduction / network resilience
positiveEvidence: Q3 net sales +4.1% YoY while adjusted EBITDA rose 24.3% and adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 27.1%.
Adjusted EPS +47.1% YoY and annual adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised.
Business is directly exposed to transmission, distribution, measurement, leak detection and pressure management rather than relying on discretionary household water spending.
Forward P/E was roughly 15x in the Aug 18 snapshot, materially less demanding than many AI/water-growth names.
risks: Volumes were slightly lower and residential construction remains soft.
Drought itself does not guarantee immediate municipal orders.
Pricing and margin expansion could normalise.
stockResearch.nextWork: Municipal backlog/order mix, federal/state water funding exposure and valuation versus historical margin regime.

positiveEvidence: One of North America's largest sulphuric-acid and spent-acid processors, with water-treatment chemicals and high-purity semiconductor acid exposure.
Q2 revenue +16.5% YoY, helped by higher merchant acid, sulphur and regen-acid pricing.
Acid segment adjusted EBITDA rose to $53.2m from $43.5m as higher selling prices more than offset higher sulphur costs.
Water Solutions revenue rose to $181.9m from $139.1m, although input-cost recovery is lagged by fixed-price contracts.
Approximate Aug 14 valuation: ~12.6x trailing P/E, ~11.4x forward P/E and ~4.3% distribution yield.
risks: Not a pure sulphur-price beneficiary because sulphur is also an input.
Water Solutions margins are temporarily squeezed by contract repricing lags.
Canadian income-fund structure, commodity cyclicality and smaller-cap liquidity.
stockResearch.nextWork: Acid contract structure, source-of-sulphur exposure, free-cash-flow coverage of distribution and sensitivity to normalised acid pricing.

stockResearch.classification: Diversified fertilizer candidate / less clean than CF
positiveEvidence: Global nitrogen market expected to stay tight in H2 2026 from disruptions, outages and strong India/Brazil import demand.
Potash remains the most affordable major nutrient and first-half potash volumes were strong.
Approximate Aug 18 valuation around 13x forward P/E and 7x EV/EBITDA.
risks: Q2 nitrogen sales volumes fell more than 25% and lower volumes offset higher prices.
Phosphate is exposed to sulphur-feedstock inflation and weak economics.
More diversified exposure means less direct capture of the US-gas/global-nitrogen arbitrage.
stockResearch.nextWork: Separate potash, nitrogen and retail earnings sensitivities rather than valuing NTR as one fertilizer beta.

positiveEvidence: Natural rubber represented 80.3% of Q2 revenue.
Q2 natural-rubber ASP rose 12.4% QoQ to the highest level in 12 years; SICOM TSR20 reached the highest level in more than 10 years in June.
Q2 natural-rubber revenue rose 16.5% QoQ.
Dual-listed exposure is available as STA in Thailand and NC2 in Singapore.
Shares traded around 0.6x book in early August.
risks: Natural-rubber sales volume fell 10.9% YoY and facility utilisation was only 50.5%.
China represented 60.2% of revenue.
The company was loss-making in 2025 and its enterprise-value/EBITDA multiple remains high despite low price-to-book.
Glove segment adds a separate cycle and raw-material/freight exposure.
stockResearch.nextWork: Q2 net-profit bridge, debt/working-capital cycle, rubber inventory accounting and sensitivity to TSR20 prices.

stockResearch.classification: Quality agriculture exposure, not a direct scarcity trade
positiveEvidence: Raised full-year adjusted profit outlook in July.
Scarcer fertilizer and water make yield-protecting genetics and precision input use more valuable over time.
risks: Q2 revenue missed estimates, seed sales were flat and crop protection sales fell 4%.
Weak crop prices and high input costs constrain farmer spending.
stockResearch.nextWork: Trait pricing, seed share and whether proprietary products can gain while farmers cut commodity inputs.

stockResearch.classification: Long-term irrigation beneficiary but near-term demand is gated
positiveEvidence: Drought and water restrictions increase the economic value of efficient irrigation.
Infrastructure business provides diversification from the farm cycle.
risks: Q2 agriculture sales fell 15.8%, North American irrigation sales fell 2.3% and international agriculture sales fell 28.9%.
Physical need is not translating into orders quickly because farm economics are weak.
stockResearch.nextWork: Wait for irrigation order inflection or policy/subsidy support rather than assuming drought alone creates near-term earnings.

falseFriends.reason: High phosphate prices look bullish, but sulphur scarcity has forced phosphate curtailments and can squeeze producer margins. Treat as a conditional recovery trade, not an automatic scarcity beneficiary.

Latest earnings strength is being driven by construction/data-centre equipment; Production & Precision Agriculture revenue still fell 6%. Do not confuse Deere's share-price strength with an agriculture-scarcity earnings inflection.
Farmers are delaying equipment purchases because fertilizer and fuel costs rose sharply. Precision-ag efficiency tools are strategically relevant, but the current farm-equipment cycle remains weak.

India's sugar import pivot is interesting for the commodity, but São Martinho's latest quarter still showed lower sugar pricing and weaker profit. Needs a fresh price/hedge/operations screen before promotion.

watchOnly.nextResearch: Screen low-cost primary aluminium producers outside disrupted Gulf capacity and quantify China-export sensitivity.

watchOnly.nextResearch: Track whether global futures reprice before Brazilian producer earnings do.

watchOnly.signal: West African supply/regulatory risks coexist with net-short speculative positioning.
watchOnly.nextResearch: No clean listed upstream equity found yet; avoid forcing chocolate manufacturers into a beneficiary bucket when cocoa inflation is a cost.

watchOnly.signal: US cattle scarcity drives record input costs, but processors can lose money when cattle costs outrun boxed-beef pricing.
watchOnly.nextResearch: Look for substitution beneficiaries rather than assuming meat processors benefit from higher beef prices.
